title: Cap. VIII: Immediate imputation needs precise actual sin
pass_a_gloss: Why skip past that admission? Garissoles answers that either way — actual sin peeled from the corruption, or actual sin still joined to it — the designation still holds, and that is enough for the immediate-imputation brief. Placeus denies the sufficiency. If the brief is immediate imputation, mere designation is not enough. What is required is imputation of actual sin as peeled from the corruption, because on that brief the corruption is the proper penalty attached to the imputed act. Otherwise one and the same sin would be punished by itself — which Placeus will not allow, least of all when speaking of a penalty in the strict sense.
pass_b_english: Why then does he not linger on that? Because, he says, whether cut off from that corruption or joined with it, it is still understood to be designated — and that is enough for our cause. No: if you are defending the cause of immediate imputation, that is not enough. Actual sin must be imputed as cut off from the corruption, if that corruption is properly the penalty of the imputed sin. For the same sin cannot be the penalty of itself — least of all a penalty properly so called.
source_text: Cur vero id non moratur? Etenim, inquit, sive praecisum ab illa corruptione, sive conjunctum cum ea, semper tamen designari intelligitur, quod ad causam nostram satis est. Immo vero si causam defendis imputationis immediatae, id non satis est. oportet enim sic imputari peccatum actuale praecisum à corruptione, siquidem haec est illius imputati poena proprie dicta. non potest enim idem peccatum esse poena sui ipsius, praesertim poena proprie dicta.

choices.decision: cut off from corruption — required for immediate view
same sin cannot be its own proper penalty
